summary: Describes a Uniform Resource Name namespace for the Digital Video Broadcasting project, used for naming persistent resources defined in its standards. These include technical documents, XML schemas, classification schemes, DTDs, namespaces, style sheets, and media assets. It is informational and was later updated.

plainLanguage.summary: The DVB Project assigns permanent names to resources defined in its standards. A name in the urn:dvb namespace can remain the same even when the resource's location changes.

questions: what is the urn dvb namespace
how are urn dvb names resolved
subtitle: A permanent URN namespace for resources defined by the DVB Project.

tldr.problem: The Digital Video Broadcasting Project needs stable names for resources such as standards, schemas, classification schemes and media assets.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC registers the URN namespace identifier dvb. DVB assigns names in the form urn:dvb followed by a namespace-specific string and maintains catalogues that map names to locations.
tldr.outcome: RFC 5328 is Informational and has been updated by RFC 7354 and RFC 8553.

today: RFC 5328 is an Informational RFC updated by RFC 7354 and RFC 8553. Consult those documents for later changes to the namespace rules.

sections.title: Why DVB Uses URNs
sections.content:
The Digital Video Broadcasting Project (DVB) wants unique, permanent, location-independent names for resources it produces or manages. The RFC describes a formal Uniform Resource Name (URN) namespace built using the URN syntax in RFC 2141.

The named resources include technical documents, eXtensible Markup Language (XML) schemas, classification schemes, document type definitions, namespaces, style sheets and media assets. A URN identifies a resource without encoding where it is stored.
sections.plainLanguage: A URN gives a resource a name that does not depend on its current location. DVB uses this namespace for resources connected with its standards.

sections.title: The urn:dvb Name Structure
sections.content:
DVB names have the form urn:dvb:<NSS>, where NSS is the namespace-specific string defined by the URN syntax. The NSS is case-insensitive, and DVB assigns each name through its standards-development process.

Only DVB and authorities it designates may assign names. DVB says assigned strings will not be reused and commits to maintaining the persistence and accessibility of officially assigned resources. The RFC's example names are explicitly not guaranteed to be real.
sections.plainLanguage: Every name begins with urn:dvb, followed by a DVB-assigned string. DVB says it will not reuse an assigned string.

sections.title: Finding a Resource from Its Name
sections.content:
DVB maintains URN catalogues that map assigned names to Uniform Resource Locators. A name is valid when it appears in a catalogue. The RFC does not prescribe one resolution method because DVB devices can have different network access and capabilities.

The document describes three ways DVB can convey resolution information: records carried repeatedly in a television broadcast stream, multicast resolution records using DVBSTP, and records returned in response to an HTTP request. To find initial service-discovery information, clients can use the registered multicast addresses and port 3937 or discover a non-default entry point through DNS SRV records.
sections.plainLanguage: A catalogue connects a DVB name to a location. A device can receive catalogue information in a broadcast or multicast stream, or request it over a network.

sections.title: Security and Registration
sections.content:
The RFC adds no security considerations beyond those associated with URNs generally. It says authentication information for a resolved resource should be carried separately from the URN, rather than embedded in the name.

IANA registered dvb in the URN Namespaces registry. The RFC requests a formal namespace because DVB publishes international standards and has a defined compliance process.
sections.plainLanguage: The URN is a name, not proof that a resource is genuine. Any authentication information should be provided separately.

references.text: Daigle, L., van Gulik, D., Iannella, R., and P. Faltstrom, "Uniform Resource Names (URN) Namespace Definition Mechanisms", BCP 66, RFC 3406, October 2002.
